item.title: Middle East live: Iranian FM says talks to finalise agreement with US 'likely' to start Friday
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Tuesday that talks on a final agreement with the United States covering Tehran's nuclear programme among other points will likely begin on Friday. Araghchi also warned that ‌any Israeli attack on Lebanon or continued presence ‌on Lebanese territory constituted a violation of the interim agreement with the United States. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Iran war 'has been a strategic disaster for the State of Israel', analyst says
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is on a collision course with Donald Trump as the US president seeks to extricate himself from the Iran war, with both men's goals unmet and Israeli military operations tied down in Lebanon. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Aaron David Miller, senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, says that "this has been a strategic disaster for the state of Israel. item.title: The Iran War Permanently Altered the Global Economy
item.description: The global order has been altered, and economies are unlikely to simply pick up where they left off before the U.S. and Israel began bombing Iran.

item.title: Netanyahu's Israel grapples with Trump-Iran deal as details remain unclear
item.description: Defense Minister Katz says IDF will remain in Lebanon security zones as Israeli leaders debate Trump-Iran deal's impact on national security interests.

item.title: Iran deal: Trump is back to square one, but the cards are now in Tehran’s favor
item.description: The signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the US and Iran on Monday has been welcomed by the international community after a devastating three-month war. The agreement was announced on June 14, President Donald Trump’s birthday, but the biggest beneficiary, experts say, is the Iranian regime.

item.title: What we know about the US-Iran memorandum of understanding
item.description: The United States and Iran, ⁠as well as mediator Pakistan, ​have provided few details about the preliminary deal announced Sunday to bring an end to the US-Iran conflict that has engulfed the region and threatened global energy supplies.

item.title: Interim US-Iran peace deal sparks anger among Israelis, who lash out at Netanyahu
item.description: Israelis from across the political spectrum reacted angrily Monday to the news of an initial deal between the U.S. and Iran, calling it a disaster for Israel and directing their fury at one man: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel to stay ‘indefinitely’ in lands seized in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria
item.description: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Monday that Israeli ground forces would remain in land they hold in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, potentially challenging a memorandum of understanding announced a day earlier between the US and Iran to end the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Israelis denounce Trump’s deal with Iran
item.description: Israeli officials disparaged the peace deal and said Israel’s fight against Hezbollah in Lebanon would go on.

item.title: Iran deal presents political nightmare for Netanyahu
item.description: Donald Trump's ceasefire agreement with Iran leaves the Israeli PM trapped in a new political and security dilemma.
